questions.question: In Britain and its colonies, the day after 2 September 1752 was officially 14 September 1752. Why did eleven days simply disappear from the calendar?
questions.answer: Switch from Julian to Gregorian calendar
questions.explanation: Britain adopted the Gregorian calendar with the Calendar (New Style) Act 1750, catching up with most of Catholic Europe, which had switched back in 1582. The older Julian calendar counted every fourth year as a leap year without exception, so it drifted about three days every four centuries against the solar year. By 1752 the gap had grown to eleven days, so Parliament ordered them dropped in one jump: people went to bed on 2 September and woke up on 14 September. The same act also moved the start of the legal year from 25 March to 1 January.
